summary: Records TOP images to movies, still images, image sequences, or stop-frame movies with codec, audio, EXR, and file-output controls.

key_params.name: videocodec
key_params.note: rle, mjpa, mpeg4, h264nvgpu, cineform, hap, h265nvgpu, gif, notchlc, vp8, vp9, prores, vvc, or av1

key_params.name: imagefiletype
key_params.note: tiff, jpeg, bmp, exr, png, or dds for image outputs

key_params.name: file
key_params.note: Output path and filename including extension

key_params.name: moviecontainer
key_params.note: automatic, mov, mp4, mkv, or webm

key_params.name: audiochop
key_params.note: Audio CHOP source to write to the output stream

key_params.name: pause
key_params.note: Pause recording; required for Add Frame stop-frame use

key_params.name: addframe
key_params.note: Add a single frame while paused

common_gotchas: H.264, H.265, and AV1 encoding require Commercial or Pro licensing; NVIDIA hardware is required on Windows.
The official audio source parameter is audiochop, not audiodevice.
Alpha output requires a codec and pixel format that support alpha.
Some codec and container combinations are invalid or unsupported.
Add Frame is for paused stop-frame workflows, not normal realtime recording.
key_concepts: Records TOP streams to movie files, single images, image sequences, or stop-frame movies.
Video codec, pixel format, and container compatibility determine what can be written.
Audio is recorded from an audiochop source and must match recording expectations.
Add Frame supports manual stop-frame and still-image workflows.
EXR output can include additional image channels and point-cloud metadata.
Non-realtime recording modes help avoid dropped frames in heavy scenes.
